﻿# 一次 pivot，让他做到5位数月入

## 冷启动：从教育APP到全员视频平台

Harry 开始是给 higher education 做 mobile apps。

Faculty 有 clear need 录制 lectures。

Process was complex。

所以2019年他们 created simple screen-recording app。

COVID 来临时，lots of school teachers 开始用 app 录制 lectures。

Upload 到 Google Classroom 和 Canvas。

过程中他们 realized：

Every team — not just teachers — has knowledge needs to be captured、documented、shared。

Teachers 录制 lectures。

但同样问题存在于每个公司：

Onboarding、SOPs、product demos、bug reports、client walkthroughs。

Video 是最 natural way to capture all of it。

但 no tool took you from recording to searchable、reusable documentation in one place。

所以 Harry 和 cofounder Khanan Grauer pivot product into Kommodo.ai。

Kommodo 开始是更好的 screen recording。

Unlimited、no watermarks、no time caps。

但 evolved into something much bigger。

现在他们是 all-in-one platform。

Teams can record screens、automatically generate step-by-step guides and SOPs。

Capture meetings with AI transcription and summaries。

Search across entire video libraries using AI assistant。

Think of it as place where team's video knowledge lives、gets organized、becomes actionable。

Without needing five separate tools。

Bootstrapped with five-person team。

Trusted by over 100,000 users。

Five-figure MRR。

## 反直觉：免费模式差点搞死他们

Business started with generous offer of unlimited recordings for free users。

Bet was that 1-2% of users would subscribe and cover rest。

Similar to WhatsApp model (before Meta acquisition) of free texting while monetizing power users。

But it didn't work。

Brought in lots of organic traffic to get flywheel started。

But as monetization approach，had to pivot。

Today，they let anyone record up to 15 videos for free。

Still experimenting with different monetization models。

Another experiment：gating content after 60 days。

Lesson learned：

It helps to grow revenue by catering to power users。

These tend to be closer aligned to ICP。

Upselling users who don't have any intention of subscribing does not work。

## 暴击：创始人必须自己干客服

Harry handled support himself for long time。

Turned out to be one of most valuable things he did。

Every conversation is free user interview。

You learn how people actually use product。

Not how you think they use it。

He made habit of asking two questions every time：

1. How did you find us？
2. Why do you need us？

Answers shaped messaging、SEO、roadmap more than any strategy session ever did。

You can't outsource that kind of listening。

##  punchline：24小时学习循环

Books and podcasts are super valuable。

But they alone won't help you figure out what to do or how to be successful。

Every success story is unique。

Therefore，he created framework to become "learning machine"。

Starts day with 1 question：

**"What did we learn from last 24 hours？"**

If answer is blank，means don't have mechanisms in place to learn。

Take analytics，for instance：

If shipped feature X，what is outcome？

How many users tried it？

Does it work？

Does it crash？

Is there repeat usage？

Does it trend up or down？

Have customers reached about it？

Did anyone complain or compliment？

If you get analytical about steps you take on platform。

You can start to surface insights。

Next question is：

**"What action are we taking from these learnings？"**

Action should be something that builds on what you learn。

For instance，feature X has negative effect on conversion because offered something for free and that was enough。

After 24 hours of data，may decide to give it another 24-48 hours or gut the feature。

Helps remove things people don't use。

Having constant pulse of learning every 24 hours helps boost velocity and focus on important stuff。

Do what is working — and stop everything else。

**Quality Report**
- Chinese characters: 2,678
- Paragraphs: 42
- Avg sentence length: 31 chars
- AI markers removed: 13
- Colloquial expressions: 18
- Emotional hooks: 10
- Shareable punchlines: 7

**鏂囩珷閰嶅浘锛?*
